title: Stablecoins and safe asset prices (BIS Working Papers No 1270)
date_evidence: May 2025 (revised February 2026) ... Stablecoins and safe asset prices* Rashad Ahmed Inaki Aldasoro February 2026
verbatim_quote: a 2-standard deviation inflow into stablecoins lowers 3-month Treasury bill yields by 2.5-3.5 basis points (bps) ... effects are statistically insignificant in periods of ample bill supply but increase to 5-8 bps during periods of bill scarcity
key_claim: Dollar stablecoin flows measurably move the short-term US Treasury market: a two-standard-deviation (~USD 3.5bn) inflow lowers 3-month T-bill yields by 2.5-3.5bps, rising to 5-8bps in periods of bill scarcity; as of December 2025 stablecoin AUM exceeded USD 270bn with USD 153bn in T-bill reserves, and issuers bought USD 33bn of T-bills in 2025, exposing the market to fire sales if a major issuer faced a run.
notes: The empirical anchor of the signal. BIS Working Paper, Monetary and Economic Department; authors Rashad Ahmed and Inaki Aldasoro. Cover 'May 2025 (revised February 2026)'; title page/abstract read February 2026 -> the single permitted structural anchor in the 3-6m band.

title: Payment Stablecoins and Cross Border Payments: Benefits and Implications for Monetary Policy Implementation (FEDS Notes)
verbatim_quote: The payment stablecoin issuer would need to back the payment stablecoin by purchasing reserve assets, and this would affect the market for those assets and everyone else that held these assets.
key_claim: Large-scale payment-stablecoin adoption shifts demand away from central-bank reserves toward Treasury bills, affecting those asset markets and carrying consequences for the central bank's balance sheet and monetary-policy implementation.
notes: Authors Kyungmin Kim and Mary-Frances Styczynski. Tier 1 central-bank source establishing the monetary-transmission framing; directional, not a point estimate.

title: Stablecoins and the future of money: separating functions from instruments (speech by Christine Lagarde)
date_evidence: meta-article:published_time: 2026-05-08 (byline: 'Speech by Christine Lagarde, President of the ECB...'; 'Roda de Bara, 8 May 2026')
verbatim_quote: Stablecoins have grown from less than USD 10 billion six years ago to more than USD 300 billion today ... nearly 90% of the market is controlled by two issuers.
key_claim: ECB President Lagarde frames stablecoins as a financial-stability and run channel: individual T-bill holdings aggregate into systemic effects, mass redemptions can trigger self-reinforcing feedback loops into asset markets (citing the SVB/USDC March 2023 de-peg to USD 0.877), and she endorses the finding that a USD 3.5bn inflow lowers 3-month T-bill yields by ~2.5-3.5bps, doubling in bill shortages.
notes: Top-tier corroboration: a sitting central-bank president endorsing the BIS T-bill price-impact finding and the run/feedback framing.

title: The Stablecoin Yield Debate (In Focus IF13174)
date_evidence: The Stablecoin Yield Debate / March 6, 2026 / IF13174 ... Revision History - Mar. 6, 2026
verbatim_quote: Stablecoins are inherently prone to run risk because of their fixed value.
key_claim: A Treasury advisory council identified USD 6.6 trillion of US transactional deposits as 'at risk' from stablecoins (with ~USD 281 billion outstanding in March 2026); Citigroup projects USD 0.5-3.7 trillion outstanding by 2030; stablecoins are 'inherently prone to run risk' and lack Fed discount-window access, raising the prospect of ad hoc bailouts as with money-market funds in 2008 and 2020.
notes: Canonical congressional primer; full text confirmed on EveryCRSReport (Congress.gov IF13174 returns no fetchable body). Bridges the deposit-competition consensus and the run-risk/safe-asset angle.

title: Stablecoins Have a Money Market Fund Problem
key_claim: Central banks at the Fed, ECB and BIS increasingly frame stablecoins as structurally analogous to money-market funds - private cash substitutes that hold tens of billions in US Treasurys and are susceptible to runs when confidence evaporates - shifting the policy question to whether the system can absorb them safely at scale.
notes: Quality payments-specialist trade journalism; confirms the 'MMF playbook' regulatory framing. Page partly gated but full body resolves below the form.

title: Stablecoins Didn't Eat the Treasury Bill Market
date_evidence: In-text citations: '"A Crypto Coin Is Gobbling Up US Treasuries," ... The New York Times, 3/8/2026' and 'Source: US Treasury, as of 3/9/2026'
verbatim_quote: Stablecoins are a drop in the bucket.
key_claim: Counter-position: the systemic-risk fear is overstated - the entire ~USD 300 billion stablecoin market is 'a drop in the bucket' against a marketable US T-bill universe of more than USD 6.8 trillion, the OCC's draft GENIUS reserve rules permit a wide pool of approved collateral beyond T-bills, and a stablecoin fire-sale is unlikely to become a systemic event 'in the time markets care about'.
notes: The explicit counter-position source. Asset-manager market commentary (Tier 3, treat directionally). No machine-readable date meta; publication ~9 March 2026 from internal citations dated 3/8/2026 and 'as of 3/9/2026'.

title: Tether Q1 2026 attestation: USD Treasury-heavy backing
date_evidence: Page dateline 'May 1, 2026'; body: 'assets backing USD token as of March 31, 2026'
verbatim_quote: direct and indirect exposure to U.S. Treasury bills amounted to approximately $141 billion ... positions Tether as the 17th largest holder of U.S. Treasuries globally.
key_claim: As of 31 March 2026, a single stablecoin issuer (Tether) reported approximately USD 141 billion of direct and indirect US Treasury-bill exposure against ~USD 183 billion of token liabilities, ranking it (by its own citation of US TIC data) the 17th-largest holder of US Treasuries globally.
notes: Tier 4 vendor/issuer self-report (BDO attestation, point-in-time, not a full audit) - used only to size one issuer's T-bill footprint, corroborating the BIS/CRS scale picture.
